$comment: The learning systems for Chapter 00 (docs/content-data.md, COURSE-PACKS.md §11): what you do in your own terminal, the chapter's objectives (quoted) and what covers them, and the reflection before the Seal (the Key Takeaways).

appTasks.title: Install GitHub Copilot CLI
steps: In a GitHub Codespace, skip this: Copilot CLI is already installed there.
On your own machine, install it one way: `npm install -g @github/copilot` (if you have Node.js), `brew install copilot-cli`, `winget install GitHub.Copilot`, or the install script.
appTasks.why: Not sure which to pick? Use `npm` if you have Node.js installed; otherwise the option that matches your system.

appTasks.title: Trust the folder and sign in
steps: Open a terminal at the root of the `copilot-cli-for-beginners` repository and run `copilot`.
Trust the folder: one time, or across all future sessions.
Type `/login`, select `Sign in with your browser (recommended)`, and select **Authorize** in your browser.
appTasks.why: The sign-in persists across sessions: you only do it once, unless your token expires or you sign out.

seen.prompt: What does Copilot CLI ask you before you sign in?
seen.explain: You’ll be asked to trust the folder containing the repository. You can trust it one time or across all future sessions.

appTasks.title: Check that it works
steps: At Copilot CLI’s prompt, type `Say hello and tell me what you can help with`.
appTasks.why: A quick test that you’re installed and signed in before the demos.

options.text: A friendly response listing what it can help with
A request to sign in again

seen.explain: Expected output: a friendly response listing Copilot CLI’s capabilities.

objectives.text: Signed in with your GitHub account
Verified it works with a simple test

reflections.prompt: Before your Seal: which of these will you use first?

choices.text: A GitHub Codespace, with everything already installed
